title: Major Shonen Jump Series Officially Ends After 5 Years With Final Release
content:
Another major long running series from Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine has now come to an end with the release of its final chapter after five years. The last couple of years have seen many of the longer running series from the end of the 2010s and early 2020s come to their respective ends . This year in particular has already seen four series end their runs with the magazine thus far, and now the fifth major title has now come to an end as 2026 starts to near its own end.

Kenta Shinohara’s Witch Watch had announced it was going to end with the manga’s next major chapter , and now that’s indeed confirmed to be the case as Witch Watch has now ended with Chapter 270. The final chapter of the series comes five years after its original debut, and features a time skip that sends Morihito, Nico and all of the others forward as fans get one final look at their wacky lives as a way to say goodbye.

Witch Watch Ends in Shonen Jump After 5 Years With Chapter 270

Witch Watch Chapter 270 officially brings Kenta Shinohara’s long running manga to an end after a year long final arc that saw Morihito and the others taking on some very tough foes. The final chapter of the series moves ahead seven years, and reveals what happened to everyone after the final battle. The group all decided to stay living together until after graduation, then went their separate ways after a while. Morihito and Nico ended up marrying and having a child together (who is nine months old by the time of the final chapter).

Kanshi took over as Tengu Leader from his father, Keigo went overseas, and Miharu’s in grad school. But the wackiness kicks back in as, one after another, the three of them all barge in the house and ask to move back in. Kanshi’s broke (due to terrible investments), Keigo’s looking for what to do next after being dumped by Nemu, and Miharu wants to form his own company to make a fortune. Morihito has since become a police officer, and Nico wants to star being a witch counselor giving advice full time. It’s teased that their child might be magical too despite seemingly not inheriting either of their abilities, but at the end of the day they’re all living together again and happily moving forward.

What’s Next for Shonen Jump After Witch Watch ?

Now that Witch Watch has come to an end after five years, it’s going to be replaced by a new series that has already made its debut in the same issue of the magazine. High School Family: Kokosei Kazoku creator Ryo Nakama has returned to Shonen Jump with the start of a brand new series after three years. Titled Jan Is in Danger! , it’s looking to be another fun comedy series that taps into the same type of vibes that made Ryo Nakama so popular before.

This is the first of three new titles coming to Shonen Jump over the rest of the month as the final wave of major updates for the year , and that means there are two other titles that are likely going to come to an end. It’s one final period of changes, so it’s time to see what ends next. How do you feel about Witch Watch ending after five years? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Manga 'Witch Watch' Concludes Serialization
content:
Kenta Shinohara 's Witch Watch manga has concluded with chapter 270 in the 51st issue of Weekly Shounen Jump magazine on Monday, after a five-year serialization.

Shinohara began serializing the supernatural comedy manga in Weekly Shonen Jump in February 2021. Shueisha published the 28th volume on October 2.

Produced by Bibury Animation Studios , the 25-episode first season aired in Spring 2025. Crunchyroll and Netflix simulcasted the anime worldwide with subtitles and dubs in multiple languages. A second season has been announced.

Viz Media licensed the manga in English in February 2022. The 19th volume went on sale on August 25. Shueisha is also publishing the manga on its Manga Plus website and app.

Synopsis Nico Wakatsuki has finished her six years of witch training and is moving back to town by herself. As a new witch, she must choose a familiar to accompany her. However, unlike the other witches, she wishes to pick a non-animal familiar. There is no better companion than Morihito "Moi" Otogi—her childhood friend who happens to be an ogre. Morihito is vehemently opposed to being her servant, but he reluctantly accepts his fate after learning that a curse would revert him into a strange cow-tiger hybrid were he to disobey a witch's order.

Due to Morihito's father leaving for a business trip and Nico's mother remaining behind in the Witches' Holy Land, the two teens find themselves living together under the same roof. While Nico is ecstatic to be living with her crush, Morihito finds that her magical antics and overall clumsiness create more problems than solutions. With a prophesied disaster to befall Nico within the year, Morihito must do everything he can to protect her as her bodyguard while also upholding his duties as her familiar. [Written by MAL Rewrite]

Official manga site: https://www.shonenjump.com/j/rensai/witch/

title: Demon Slayer Gets a Major Future Update For the Next 100 Years (But There’s a Catch)
content:
Aniplex and Sony Entertainment have major plans to keep Demon Slayer relevant for the next 100 years, but there’s a huge problem with this plan that can’t be ignored. Written and illustrated by Koyoharu Gotouge, the manga began serialization in the Weekly Shonen Jump Magazine in 2016 and reached its conclusion four years later. While the manga was already decently popular, the anime adaptation by Ufotable helped it reach new heights of popularity. The striking visuals, soundtrack, and overall adaptation by Ufotable are among the best in the industry, which is why the series continues to rise in popularity.

The first installment of the Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle trilogy made history after crossing the 100 billion yen milestone worldwide, becoming the first Japanese film ever to do so. The franchise will adapt the rest of the Infinity Castle Arc in two more movies, although there hasn’t been any confirmation regarding the adaptation of the Sunrise Countdown Arc. While fans await updates on the second part of the movie , Atsuhiro Iwakami, president of Sony Music Entertainment Japan and chairman of Aniplex, Sony’s anime production company, shares his plans for the future of Demon Slayer.

Aniplex Plans to Make Demon Slayer Last for the Next 100 Years

According to Bloomberg via The Japan Times , Iwakami shared, “With Demon Slayer, it is our intent to make this last 10 or 20, if not 50 to 100 years.” He also adds, “We want to make sure we’re part of creating the type of franchise that can withstand decades.” Iwakami specifically mentions Dragon Ball and One Piece , stories that have survived for decades, long enough for parents and their children to be fans of. Sony has the streaming rights to both of these legendary anime, which is all the more reason why they have similar plans for Demon Slayer .

Long-running franchises such as Dragon Ball and One Piece are often carried by nostalgia and new releases, as they raised entire generations of Shonen fans. These stories are timeless classics, and it’s almost a given that fans will always have a soft spot for them. On the other hand, Demon Slayer is way too new compared to them, but it’s still one of the most popular Shonen of all time.

Last recorded in July 2025, Demon Slayer has sold over 220 million copies of manga, ranking seventh among the best-selling manga series of all time. The popularity only keeps rising, and it wouldn’t be surprising if it surpassed Naruto (250 million copies) and Dragon Ball (260 million copies). However, there’s one major drawback with Demon Slayer compared to Shonen classics.

Demon Slayer is a Shorter Story Compared to Dragon Ball and One Piece

The main reason why these two Shonen classics maintained their global fan base through several decades is that they are rather long-running stories. One Piece is still ongoing, and the anime is more popular than ever thanks to its stunning visuals in recent years. Not to mention that the series has released several non-canon movies over the years, and it also announced its first-ever canon movie, God Valley, this year. The story is in its Final Saga, and it will take at least a few years for it to reach a conclusion. Even after the finale, the expansive world-building and dozens of fan-favorite characters ensure that the series will always keep releasing new content.

The fact that One Piece already has several official spin-offs, written by different authors, is a testament to its lasting legacy. The same can be said about Dragon Ball , which has released manga sequels, several anime series, spin-offs, and movies over the past forty years. Even now, fans are anticipating the anime’s return with the Galactic Patrol Saga and the manga’s return with Toyotaro taking over the helm.

Compared to them, Demon Slayer is a much shorter story with rarely any spin-offs or non-canon stories. The world-building isn’t impressive, and the manga’s ending made sure that there isn’t any room for the story to expand . Not to mention it’s been more than six years since the finale, but Gotouge has no plans for returning with a new spin-off or even another story. With this in mind, it will be difficult for Sony to keep the series relevant for decades if all they have is around 200 chapters of the manga.

Do you wish Demon Slayer had a longer story to explore its world? What would you like to see covered in the next few decades after the anime is concluded? Share your thoughts in the comments!

title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- TV Anime Gets 5th Season
content:
Kadokawa revealed on Saturday at a 10th anniversary event for the Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- anime that the anime will get a fifth season. The company also revealed an "ultra teaser visual" for the new season. Update: Replaced ultra teaser visual with English version.

The fourth season consisted of 19 episodes divided into two arcs. The season debuted with "The Loss Arc" on April 8. Then, "The Recapture Arc" began on August 12. Crunchyroll is streaming the anime.

The 25-episode first anime season of Tappei Nagatsuki 's Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- light novel series premiered in April 2016. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired in Japan.

Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Director's Cut , an updated version of the television anime's first season, premiered in January 2020. The new edit of the first 25-episode season adds some new footage and reworks the episodes to run in a one-hour timeslot. Crunchyroll is streaming the anime.

Crunchyroll is also streaming both the Re:Zero ~Starting Break Time From Zero~ and Re:PETIT ~Starting Life in Another World from PETIT~ short anime spinoff series. Funimation released the television anime on home video with an English dub in June 2018.

The anime has inspired two original video anime ( OVA ) volumes, titled Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Memory Snow and Re:ZERO - Starting Life in Another World - The Frozen Bond . Crunchyroll is streaming both anime.

The anime's second season premiered in July 2020. The second season's latter half premiered in January 2021. Crunchyroll streamed the second season as it aired in Japan.

The third season's "Shūgeki-hen" (Attack Arc) debuted in October 2024 with a 90-minute special. The "Hangeki-hen" (Counterattack Arc) then debuted in February 2025. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired. Each arc had eight episodes.

Nagatsuki launched the story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website in 2012. Yen Press is publishing the light novel series in English, and is also releasing Daichi Matsuse 's manga adaptation of the series, as well as the Re:Zero Ex spinoff light novel series. The overall franchise has more than 16 million copies in circulation worldwide (including digital copies).

title: Uzono Shiniko Hōkoku Manga Ends in 4th Volume
content:
Kadokawa is listing the fourth volume of Gonbe Shinkawa 's Uzono Shiniko Hōkoku (Uzono Shiniko Report) manga as the final volume for the series. The volume will ship on January 7.

The manga is about the informal investigation carried out by the Japanese government, the military, investigative agencies, and ordinary citizens since 1892, about the strange phenomena called "Uzono Shiniko." It is said that if a human, animal, or any inanimate object's name is changed to "Uzono Shiniko," it suddenly attracts disaster.

Shinkawa launched the series on Kadokawa 's ComicWalker manga website in December 2024. The manga is an adaptation of Bunkichi Majima 's novel of the same title. Asahiro Kakashi is credited for the manga's storyboard composition.

Dai Chikamoto and Shinkawa launched the The Witch and the Knight Will Survive ( Majo to Kishi wa Ikinokoru ) manga on Kadokawa 's Young Ace Up website in June 2021. The manga ended in its third compiled book volume, which shipped in Japan in October 2023. Yen Press published the manga's final volume in English in October 2024.

Yen Press is also releasing Shinkawa and Shien Bis ' The Wolf Never Sleeps manga and Shinkawa and Yuba Isukari 's Yokohama Station SF manga in English.
author: ANN

title: Odekake Kozame Anime Gets 2nd Film
content:
The second episode of the online radio program SameRadi! announced on Sunday that the anime of Penguin Box 's Odekake Kozame (Little Shark's Outings) manga will have a second film. The staff presented a teaser trailer and a teaser visual for Eiga Odekake Kozame Mizu no Machi no Omoide (Little Shark's Outings the Movie: Memories of the Water Town):

Director Chihiro Kumano and character designer Ayumi Takeuchi are returning from the project's first film and second net anime season, and scriptwriter Hiroaki Nagashima and the ENGI animation studio are also returning from all previous anime titles in the franchise . Three cast members — Kana Hanazawa (Kozame-chan), Megumi Han (Anko-chan), and Misaki Kuno (Usame-chan) — gave messages to celebrate the announcement of the new film.

The manga and its anime adaptations follow the nostalgic everyday adventures of a young shark.

Penguin Box debuted the manga on X (formerly Twitter ) in June 2021. The manga's eighth compiled book volume shipped in Japan on March 16.

The manga's first anime adaptation premiered on YouTube in August 2023, and its 60th and final episode streamed in May 2024. The anime also aired on television.

The first film, Eiga Odekake Kozame Tokai no Otomodachi opened in Japan in August 2025. The film centers on the titular character Kozame-chan's trip to the city, when she sees a glittering poster of the city in front of the Yaocho's train station. Dazed by a shark-shaped cloud, Kozame-chan boards the train and heads to the bright, noisy, crowded city, and starts a big adventure.

The second, ongoing season premiered on April 12 on TV Tokyo and its affiliates inside the Animori! program, which airs at 7:00 a.m. JST. The season also streams on YouTube starting on April 12 at 7:05 a.m. JST.

title: WEBTOON CEO Junkoo Kim Receives Outstanding Contribution Award at Korea's 26th Cartoon Day Ceremony
content:
WEBTOON Entertainment CEO Junkoo Kim received an outstanding contribution award for his contributions to the development of the webtoon industry at the 26th Cartoon Day ceremony, held on November 3 at the Korea Manhwa Museum in Bucheon, South Korea.

The Korea Manhwa Contents Agency announced the award recipients on November 5. Kim shared the award with attorney Sung-joo Kim of law firm Deoksu, who was recognized for his work protecting cartoonists' rights and providing legal support.

Twelve major industry organizations jointly organized the ceremony, including the Korea Cartoonists Association and the Cartoon and Webtoon Associations Federation. It recognized the cultural significance of Korean comics and acknowledged creators' work.

The event also included a talk concert on the present and future of print comics, with discussions covering independent publishing, production and distribution models, creator-led publishing, and support policies for diverse comics. Awards were also presented in three categories: the Korea Comics Critics Contest, the Korea Creative Comics Contest, and Today's Korean Comics .

Cartoon Day commemorates the November 3, 1996, rally at Seoul's Yeouido Plaza, where cartoonists gathered to oppose comics censorship and defend freedom of expression.

Korea Manhwa Contents Agency Chairman Kwan-je Cho said the global standing of Korean comics and webtoons reflects the dedication of earlier generations of cartoonists and the passion of current creators. He added that the agency would continue supporting the industry and its efforts to expand internationally.

title: Stranger Than Heaven Game Streams Story Trailer for 2nd Act 'Kure'
content:
Sega began streaming a story trailer for Ryu ga Gotoku Studio's Stranger Than Heaven game (previously codenamed "Project Century") on Friday. The video outlines the game's second act "Kure," and highlights the protagonist Makoto Daito's life in 1929 in Kure.

A previous trailer outlined the game's first act.

The game will explore different times and places in Japan's modern history, including Kokura, Fukuoka in 1915; Kure, Hiroshima in 1929; Minami, Osaka in 1943; Atami, Shizuoka in 1951; and the fictional neighborhood of Kamurocho (based on the Kabukicho neighborhood, and a constant setting of RGG Studio's Yakuza/Like a Dragon games) in Shinjuku, Tokyo in 1965.

Sega describes the game's story:

A 50-year saga of those with nowhere to go and their desperate struggle to find a home. In 1915 San Francisco, a young boy, Makoto Daito, sneaks aboard a suspicious ship in the harbor under the cover of night. Born to an American father and a Japanese mother, Makoto faces harsh persecution due to his Asian heritage. After losing both of his parents, Makoto decides to travel to his mother's homeland, Japan, where a fateful encounter awaits. With nothing but the shirt on his back, Makoto soon learns, however, that his voyage across the Pacific is anything but a "free ride," and that this one choice will forever change the course of his life.

The cast includes:

• Yū Shirota as Makoto Daito

• Snoop Dogg as Orpheus

• Moeka Hoshi as Tae Matsumoto

• Tori Kelly as Suzy Day

• Akio Ōtsuka as Heigo Yashima

• Tokuma Nishioka as Kiyoshi Otsuru

• Satoshi Fujihara as Takashi

• Cordell Broadus as The Veiled Stranger

• Ado as Keiko Shirai

• Bunta Sugawara (model basis) and Takashi Ukaji (voice) as Genzo Iwaki

• Late American rapper Tupac

• Takaya Kuroda (who plays Kazuma Kiryu in Ryu ga Gotoku's related Yakuza/Like a Dragon series)

• Kouhei Tsuji

• Yasukaze Motomiya (who plays Kosei Shishido in the Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name game and Kazuma Kiryu in Nihon Tohitsu's live-action Like a Dragon Powered By Nihon Touitsu series)

Sega provided the following comment regarding the character Genzo Iwaki and the model for the character being based on the late actor Bunta Sugawara :

In STRANGER THAN HEAVEN , the late and legendary actor Bunta Sugawara appears. SEGA received formal consent from his family, and, with materials provided by Toei Company Ltd. —which produced many of Mr. Sugawara's films, including the Battles Without Honor and Humanity — RGG Studio crafted his CG character design based on archival footage and photographs from the time.

Snoop Dogg , Satoshi Fujihara , Ado, and Tori Kelly perform the game's theme song "Stranger Than Heaven." The song will get a release this year.

The game is inspiring a live-action film on Netflix .

Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties , Ryu ga Gotoku Studio's remake of the Yakuza 3 game along with the new standalone Dark Ties title, launched as a single release for PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam worldwide on February 12.

title: MyGO and Ave Mujica Anime Sequel Unveils 2nd Trailer Featuring MyGO
content:
A second trailer was unveiled for the upcoming anime sequel to MyGO and Ave Mujica, titled BanG Dream! MyGO!!!!! // Ave Mujica . The latest trailer mainly features the MyGO and the anime is slated to premiere on January 8, 2027. An Ave Mujica focused video was previously released last month.

The voice cast will reprise their roles for the sequel:

• Hina Youmiya as Tomori Takamatsu

• Kanon Takao as Sakiko Togawa/Oblivionis

• Rin Tateishi as Anon Chihaya

• Mika Kohinata as Soyo Nagasaki

• Yuzuki Watase as Mutsumi Wakaba/Mortis

• Coco Hayashi as Taki Shina

• Rico Sasaki as Uika Misumi/Doloris

• Hina Aoki as Rana Kaname

• Akane Yonezawa as Nyamu Yutenji/Amoris

• Mei Okada as Umiri Yahata/Timoris

• Hazuki Tanda as Mana Sumita

Muse Asia is streaming both BanG Dream! It’s MyGO!!!!! and Ave Mujica: The Die is Cast . They describe the former as follows: “Would you play in a band for your whole life?” Late spring of the first year of high school. Everyone at Haneoka Girls’ High School is in a band. Anon, who enrolled in school late, rushes to find band members so she can fit in with her classmates as soon as possible. While at it, she learned that Tomori, the “Haneoka’s Weirdo Girl”, has not yet formed a band. And then, Anon calls on her… The scream of our music may be covered in scars and ill-formed. Even if we get lost, just move forward.
author: Anime Corner

title: RetroCrush Streams Sugar Sugar Rune, Genocyber Anime
content:
The service has also now added many of the titles it had announced in August that it was adding from Viz Media , including: Vampire Knight , Accel World , Naruto the Movie: Ninja Clash in the Land of Snow , Sailor Moon R: The Movie , Bleach the Movie: Hell Verse , and Captain Tsubasa . The service will add Hunter × Hunter: Phantom Rouge on November 20 and Hikaru no Go on November 27.

RetroCrush had added Vampire Princess Miyu with a Japanese dub on October 2 and with an English dub on October 30.

Discotek Media released Genocyber on Blu-ray Disc in January 2021. The anime is based on Tony Takezaki 's manga.

The Sugar Sugar Rune anime debuted in July 2005 and the Tubi service began streaming the series in January of this year. The anime is based on Moyoco Anno 's manga that was serialized in Kodansha 's Nakayoshi magazine from 2004 to 2007.

Cult Epics most recently released The Girl Who Leapt Through Time on Blu-ray Disc on January 20 earlier this year. Nobuhiko Ōbayashi directed the film with a script by Wataru Kenmotsu . The movie is based on the same novel by Yasutaka Tsutsui that inspired Mamoru Hosoda 's 2006 anime film.
author: ANN
